exposure: history of urinary tract infection or sexually transmitted infection
low APGAR score in the fifth minute
cohort: 264 neonates (66 cases with neonatal sepsis and 198 controls without) admitted to Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital and Adare General Hospital between April and June 2018.
finding: Prolonged rupture of membranes, intrapartum fever, history of urinary tract infection or sexually transmitted infection during pregnancy, foul-smelling amniotic fluid, and low APGAR score at five minutes were independent risk factors for neonatal sepsis.
